'''Damien Leo Leith''' (born 18 January 1976, in [[Dublin]]) is an Irish-Australian [[singer–songwriter]]. He was the winner of the [[Network Ten]] music contest ''[[Australian Idol (season 4)|Australian Idol]]'' in 2006. Since winning the title, Leith has released nine studio albums, four of which peaked in the top two of the [[ARIA]] Charts, including two number ones. He has been awarded seven platinum and one gold certification for albums and singles by [[ARIA]], which equates to sales of just over half a million.<ref>[http://www.aria.com.au/pages/aria-charts-accreditations.htm Album and Single Accreditations 1997–2013] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721044303/http://www.aria.com.au/pages/aria-charts-accreditations.htm |date=21 July 2011 }}. Australian Recording Industry Association. Retrieved 24 January 2012.</ref>

==Early life==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=November 2022}}
As a teenager Leith formed a family band, "Leaf", with his sister Áine and brothers Paul and Darren. Leaf recorded in [[New York City]] and then again later under the new name "Releaf", which made an appearance in the Irish Top 100. After moving to [[Sydney]], he played in a number of high-profile venues, as front-man for a band known as ''Revelate''. His first Australian performance was at The Basement in Sydney's [[Circular Quay]].

Before auditioning for ''[[Australian Idol]]'', Leith worked in Sydney as a [[chemist]] with Pharmalab utilising the [[Bachelor of Science]] ([[Honours degree|Honours]]) in [[Chemistry]] he obtained from [[University College, Dublin]] and [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] experience within the Metallosupramolecular Research Group in the Chemistry Department of [[Trinity College, Dublin]].

==''Australian Idol'' 2006==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=November 2022}}
Only following determined coaxing by friends, Leith auditioned for the 4th series of [[Network Ten]]'s [[Australian Idol]] along with some 25,000 other contestants. He was selected by the judges as one of the final 24 contestants, and was the first person voted into the competition's top 12 as the result of a nationwide viewer vote. He was praised by the show's judges for his [[falsetto]] technique, which he used regularly in performances. For the first time, Australian Idol 2006 permitted contestants to perform with instruments, and Leith accompanied himself on guitar for his renditions of [[Chris Isaak]]'s "[[Wicked Game]]", [[Leonard Cohen]]'s "[[Hallelujah (Leonard Cohen song)|Hallelujah]]", [[Alex Lloyd]]'s "Never Meant to Fail" and [[Ben Harper]]'s "Waiting on an Angel", and on piano for his rendition of [[Split Enz]]'s "Message to My Girl". Leith also played piano for the non-competition round "Up Close and Personal" night, when he performed his original song "Sky".{{Citation needed|date=September 2010}}

Despite adverse comments from judges [[Mark Holden]] and [[Kyle Sandilands]] in relation to Leith's appearance and a performance of [[Kool and the Gang]]'s "Celebration" on the "Disco" theme night, which drew ridicule from Holden, the judges' assessments of Leith's performances were usually positive with Holden labelling him a 'darkhorse' early in the competition. His renditions of [[Chris Isaak]]'s "[[Wicked Game]]", [[Roy Orbison]]'s "[[Crying (Roy Orbison song)|Crying]]", [[Leonard Cohen]]'s "[[Hallelujah (Leonard Cohen song)|Hallelujah]]" and [[Giacomo Puccini|Puccini]]'s "[[Nessun Dorma]]" each earned Leith a "Touchdown" from Mark Holden, Holden's ultimate accolade for an excellent performance. {{Citation needed|date=September 2010}}

Leith holds the record (with [[Australian Idol 2004]] winner [[Casey Donovan (singer)|Casey Donovan]]) for being awarded the most touchdowns, at four apiece. Sandilands also stated that the family of Roy Orbison had contacted the ''Australian Idol'' producers requesting a copy of Leith's performance of "Crying". Although he was one of the most popular interviewees on Idol's behind-the-scenes show [[Idol Backstage]], he was not expected by betting agencies to win the competition with [[Dean Geyer]] punted as the favourite to win throughout.

Leith is one of only few contestants to never land in the bottom 2 or bottom 3 throughout their series. During a live broadcast from the [[Sydney Opera House]], Leith was announced the winner, over runner-up [[Jessica Mauboy]]. At age 30 at the time, Leith became the second oldest winner of any Idol series in the world. Controversy among viewers was created as Leith was not an [[Australians|Australian]] [[Citizenship|citizen]] at the time of winning the ''[[Australian Idol]]''. {{Citation needed|date=September 2010}}

==Post-''Idol'' career==
===2006: ''The Winner's Journey''===
Leith signed a recording contract with [[Sony BMG]] and his debut single, "[[Night of My Life (Damien Leith song)|Night of My Life]]", was released as a paid digital download from [[Bigpond|Bigpond Music]] soon after the conclusion of the grand finale, with an official CD release on 28 November, which included an original composition written and produced by Leith titled "Come to Me".

The single was certified "Gold" (35,000 copies sold) within 72 hours of its release.<ref name="Gold Accreditation">{{cite web|title='Night of My Life' Goes Gold!|url=http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829003972|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061222163252/http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829003972|archive-date=22 December 2006|access-date=29 November 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 3 December 2006, the single debuted at number 1 and stayed in that position for 4 weeks, being accredited [[Music recording sales certification|Platinum]] (70,000 copies shipped) in its first week of release. It was the fastest-selling debut single released during 2006, and also the most added song to radio.<ref name="Single Debut">{{cite web|title=Damien Leith - Latest News|url=http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829003996|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061216020335/http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829003996|archive-date=16 December 2006|access-date=5 December 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref> The video for "[[Night of My Life (Damien Leith song)|Night of My Life]]" debuted on national television on Saturday 9 December 2006. Set in the urban streets of [[Chippendale, New South Wales]], the video was produced by Cutting Edge Productions.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

Although with an official release date of 9 December, on 6 December 2006, Leith's CD/DVD pack entitled ''[[The Winner's Journey (Damien Leith album)|The Winner's Journey]]'' with all his ''[[Australian Idol|Idol]]'' performances and two original tracks began appearing in non-[[Australian Record Industry Association|ARIA]] accredited stores. The release debuted at number 3 with [[Music recording sales certification|Platinum accreditation]] (70,000 copies shipped) on the [[Australian Record Industry Association|ARIA]] Album Charts released on Sunday, 10 December 2006, and rose to number 1 on the following week, with 89,000 units sold and certified platinum four times (280,000 copies shipped).{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} It sold a 2006 record of 101,206 units in the pre-[[Christmas]] week and continued to stay in the same position of number 1 for the next four weeks.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

In late December 2006, Leith signed with Sony BMG Ireland and, on 18 January 2007, "Night of My Life" entered the Top 10 singles chart in [[Ireland]].<ref name="Ireland Chart">{{cite web|title=Ireland-Top Singles Chart|url=http://allcharts.org/music/ireland/singles.htm|access-date=22 January 2006}}</ref> The next week it rose up two spots to the position of number 8. Leith performed in a nationally televised concert, Australia Day Live, on the eve of [[Australia Day]] in 2007, in the nation's capital, [[Canberra]]. He performed two songs, [[Peter Allen (musician)|Peter Allen]]'s "Tenterfield Saddler" with the Canberra Symphony Orchestra, and "Night of My Life".{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

In late February 2007, Leith embarked on a two-week, 14 show tour of major Australian East Coast cities.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} Labelled ''The Winner's Journey Tour'', the concerts featured many of the songs performed by Leith during Australian Idol, as well as showcasing new original songs destined for his forthcoming studio album, including the folk/acoustic piece "Song for Jarvis", dedicated to his son, and "Beautiful", a band piece written by Leith during his trip to Ireland after winning ''Australian Idol''. Supporting Leith on the tour was Sydney singer-songwriter and friend [[Mark Wilkinson (singer)|Mark Wilkinson]].{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

On 22 February 2007, Leith was presented with two [[Australian Record Industry Association|ARIA]] No. 1 Chart Awards for his first single "Night of My Life" and first album ''[[The Winner's Journey (Damien Leith album)|The Winner's Journey]]''. These awards are presented to Australian artists whose singles and albums reach no. 1 on the [[Australian Record Industry Association|ARIA]] national single and album charts over the thirteen months from December 2005 to December 2006.

In March 2007, Leith again performed "Night of My Life" and was nominated for "Spankin' New Artist" and "Best Male Artist" awards at the [[MTV Australia Video Music Awards 2007]].

On 9 July 2007, Leith was nominated for a 2007 Helpmann Award in the category of Best Performance in an Australian Contemporary Concert (other nominees are [[David Campbell (Australian musician)|David Campbell]], [[Kylie Minogue]] and [[Olivia Newton-John]]). The annual Helpmann Awards recognise distinguished artistic achievement and excellence in the many disciplines of Australia's vibrant live performance sectors, including musical theatre, contemporary music, comedy, opera, classical music, dance and physical theatre. The Helpmann Awards, named in honour of Sir [[Robert Helpmann]] and to commemorate his memory and achievements, are similar to the [[Tony Award]]s on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] and the Olivier Awards in London. In early November 2007, Leith performed "22 Steps" on the TV soap opera ''[[Neighbours]]''.

===2007–2008: ''Where We Land''===
Leith's second single "[[22 Steps]]" was released to Australian radio on 22 June 2007 and then was in stores on 21 July,<ref name="22 Steps">{{cite web|title=Tune in This Friday for the Radio Debut of Damien's New Single '22 Steps'|url=http://www.sonymusic.com.au/news/details.do?newsId=20030829004650|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070902141500/http://www.sonymusic.com.au/news/details.do?newsId=20030829004650|archive-date=2 September 2007|access-date=19 June 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> which debut and peaked at number 11 on the ARIA Singles Chart. The studio album ''[[Where We Land]]'' followed and was released on 18 August 2007. It debuted at number one on 27 August in the [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]] Albums Chart. This is his second number one album within seven months. Damien is also the first [[Australian Idol]] winner to score two consecutive number 1 albums.<ref name="''Idol's'' Damien Leith debuts at No.1">{{cite news |title=''Idol's'' Damien Leith debuts at No.1 |url=http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/story/0,23663,22313991-5000660,00.html |access-date=27 August 2007 |agency=AAP |date=27 August 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070917050349/http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/story/0%2C23663%2C22313991-5000660%2C00.html |archive-date=17 September 2007 }}</ref> Leith had an appearance on ''[[Rove (TV series)|Rove]]'' on 26 August 2007<ref name="Damien Leith on Rove">{{cite web|title=Damien Leith on Rove |url=http://www.rovedaily.com.au/the-show-guest-damian-leith.htm |access-date=27 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070826220327/http://www.rovedaily.com.au/the-show-guest-damian-leith.htm |archive-date=26 August 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and he performed live during the semi-finals of [[Australian Idol 2007]] on 30 August.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Journey Continues|url=http://www.australianidol.com.au/news-damien-leith-performance-semi-finals.html|access-date=26 August 2007}}</ref> The second single from the album is "All I Want Is You",<ref name="Perth+AdelaideTour">[http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829005023 Damien To Include Perth + Adelaide In His Tour!] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027131014/http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829005023 |date=27 October 2007 }}. [[Sony BMG]]. Retrieved on 28 September 2007.</ref> which he performed on 8 October verdict show on [[Australian Idol 2007]].

Leith embarked on a national ''Where We Land'' tour around Australia, performing his own material from the album, which began in November.<ref name="Damien Leith packs his bags!">{{cite web|title= Damien Leith packs his bags!|url=http://www.australianidol.com.au/news-damien-leith-tour.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070831105633/http://www.australianidol.com.au/news-damien-leith-tour.html|archive-date=31 August 2007|access-date=10 August 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> The original schedule of the tour only included venues located along the east coast, but it was announced on 28 September that the tour will be extended to include [[Adelaide]] and [[Perth]].<ref name="Perth+AdelaideTour"/>

During February 2007, Leith signed a book deal with Australian publishers, [[HarperCollins]]. His first novel, written three years before entering ''Australian Idol'', has been described by Leith as a psychological thriller set in Nepal. The novel, ''One More Time'', was released on 1 October 2007.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071012164410/http://damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829004957 "Damien Leith To Release Novel!"]. [[Sony BMG]]. Retrieved on 28 September 2007</ref>

In October 2007, Leith was nominated for three Australian [[ARIA Music Awards of 2007|ARIA Music Awards]] including; Best Breakthrough Single and Highest Selling Single for "[[Night of My Life (Damien Leith song)|Night of My Life]]", which he was unsuccessful in. He was also nominated for Highest Selling Album for ''[[The Winner's Journey (Damien Leith album)|The Winner's Journey]]'', which he won.

In February 2008, Damien began hosting [[Network Ten]]'s television series ''Saving Kids''. It was filmed at [[Sydney Children's Hospital]], allowing viewers to see medical miracles unfolding in the stories of children being treated for serious illnesses and horrific injuries. His song "Not Just for the Weekend" from his debut studio album served as the theme song and was released as a promotional single to promote the show.<ref name="Cheaper thrills">{{cite news|title= Cheaper thrills|url=https://www.theage.com.au/entertainment/cheaper-thrills-20080117-ge6m40.html|access-date=17 January 2008|location=Melbourne|work=The Age|date=17 January 2008}}</ref>

===2008: ''Catch the Wind''===
On 26 April 2008, less than a year after the release of his first studio album, ''[[Where We Land]]'', Leith released his second album, ''[[Catch the Wind: Songs of a Generation]]''. The album contained his own interpretations of classic folk songs.

The album debut in the [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]] Albums Chart at number 3 on 4 May and rose to its peak at number 2 the next week held off the top spot by [[André Rieu]] and [[Mirusia]]'s ''[[Waltzing Matilda (album)|Waltzing Matilda]]''. It was certified Gold in its third week. Leith performed a series of live shows across Australia for his Catch the Wind tour which began in May and ran until late July. The tour was up-close and personal set in small venues with only two other band members.<ref name="Damien Announces 'Catch The Wind' Aussie Tour!">{{cite web|title= Catch The Wind Tour|url=http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829005459|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719154225/http://www.damienleith.com.au/newsEvents/home.do?newsId=20030829005459|archive-date=19 July 2008|access-date=10 June 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2009: ''Remember June''===
Leith's third studio album, ''[[Remember June]]'', was released in Australia on 9 October. It debuted at number 25 and spent two weeks in the ARIA Top 50 Albums Chart, and 3 weeks in the ARIA Top 20 Australian Artist Albums Chart.<ref>[http://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Damien+Leith&titel=Remember+June&cat=a Australian-Charts Damien Leith Remember June] Retrieved 15 November 2009</ref><ref>[http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_album.asp?chart=1G50 ariacharts.com.au ARIA Top 50 Albums Chart] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111127023332/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_album.asp?chart=1G50 |date=27 November 2011 }} Retrieved 17 November 2009</ref><ref>[http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_australian.asp?chart=1U20AUS&chart2=1A20AUS aria.com.au ARIA Top 20 Australian Singles & Albums Charts] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216054251/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_australian.asp?chart=1U20AUS&chart2=1A20AUS |date=16 December 2008 }} Retrieved 17 November 2009</ref> The first single from the album, "To Get to You", went to radio on 14 September, and was released 25 September. The second single "Forgive Forget" was released in April 2010. It reached No. 65 on the ARIA Singles Chart, No. 1 on the ARIA Physical Singles Chart,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_physical_singles.asp?chart%3D1S50 |title=Top 50 Physical Singles Chart - Australian Record Industry Association |access-date=7 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100311184000/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_physical_singles.asp?chart=1S50 |archive-date=11 March 2010 }} Retrieved 11 April 2010</ref> and No. 13 on the Australian Artists Single Chart.<ref>[http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_australian.asp?chart=1U20AUS&chart2=1A20AUS ARIA Charts ARIA Top 20 Australian Singles ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216054251/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_australian.asp?chart=1U20AUS&chart2=1A20AUS |date=16 December 2008 }} Retrieved 18 April 2010</ref>
He has also released his second novel which has a father and son relationship plot, and was released by HarperCollins. The book is also called ''Remember June''. His first novel, "One More Time" was published in 2007.<ref name="Folk idol">{{cite news|title= Folk idol|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/music/sebastian-fills-some-big-shoes/2008/03/02/1204402257794.html|access-date=3 March 2008|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=3 March 2008}}</ref>

===2011: ''Roy''===
In an interview with Australian magazine ''New Idea'', Damien mentioned he had recorded his fourth studio album in the United States. It was released on 15 April 2011. It is an album of [[Roy Orbison]] covers, entitled ''Roy'', and was released to coincide with what would have been Orbison's 75th birthday. This album was produced by [[Barbara Orbison]], Roy's widow, who died on 6 December 2011, aged 61. The album peaked at number 2, and spent 25 non-consecutive weeks on the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Top 50 Albums Chart]] and gained platinum certification.<ref>[http://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Damien+Leith&titel=Roy+%2D+A+Tribute+To+Roy+Orbison&cat=a Damien Leith - Roy]. ARIA Chart Archives. Hung Medien. Retrieved 29 December 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_album.asp?chart=1G50Top 50 Albums Chart - Australian Recording Industry Association]{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]]. Retrieved 25 April 2011.</ref>

===2012–2014: ''Now & Then'' and ''Chapter Seven''===
On Friday, 20 April 2012, Damien's fifth studio album ''[[Now & Then (Damien Leith album)|Now & Then]]'' was released. It debuted at number 14 and peaked at number 12 on the [[ARIA Charts]], and spent four weeks in the top 50. Two singles, "Beautiful" and "Run", were released. Neither single impacted on the ARIA Charts. "Beautiful" was featured in an Estee Lauder TV commercial airing on various networks in the United States in late 2012.

On 1 November 2013, Damien's released a new album called ''[[Chapter Seven (album)|Chapter Seven]]''. It was preceded by single "Without a Fight", which was released on 13 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/chapter-seven/698804251|title=Chapter Seven by Damien Leith|website=[[iTunes]] |date=1 November 2013|access-date=14 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/without-a-fight-single/691866047|title=Without a Fight - Single by Damien Leith|website=[[iTunes]] |date=13 September 2013|access-date=14 April 2018}}</ref> ''Chapter Seven'' spent one week in the ARIA Top 100, peaking at number 57.<ref name="ARIA Report">[https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20131123130000/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/23790/20131124-0000/Issue%201238.pdf The ARIA Report: Week commencing 18 November 2013]{{cbignore|bot=medic}}. Pandora Archives. Retrieved 7 December 2013</ref> Its three singles, "Without a Fight", "Halfway Heart" and "You and I" did not chart.

In May 2014, Leith released a new single titled "One and Only Mum".<ref name="iTunes Australia">{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/au/album/one-and-only-mum-single/876003998|title=Damien Leith - One And Only Mum - Single|date=8 May 2014 |publisher=iTunes Australia|access-date=22 February 2015}}</ref>

In August 2014, Leith released a triple A-sided single of "Last Goodbye"/"Fields of Gold"/"Girl Back on Blue Bayou" via Leithal Enterprises with [[Joe Melson]].<ref name="itunes.apple.com">{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/au/album/damien-leith-and-joe-melson-single/908483435|title=Damien Leith and Joe Melson - Single|date=2 August 2014 |publisher=iTunes Australia|access-date=21 November 2014}}</ref>

In November 2014, Leith released a Christmas [[extended play]] titled ''It's Christmas Time''. It featured the traditional Christmas carols "Silent Night", "Jingle Bells", "It's Christmas Time", "Auld Lang Syne" and "Deck the Halls".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/au/album/its-christmas-time-ep/944003736|title= It's Christmas Time EP|date= 20 November 2014|publisher=iTunes Australia|access-date=21 February 2015}}</ref>

===2015-2017: ''Songs from Ireland''===
In February 2015, Leith announced his eighth album titled ''[[Songs from Ireland]]''. The release reunites him with Sony Music Australia as he covers classic Irish songs including "Molly Malone", "Galway Girl" and "Wild Colonial Boy" and was released in March.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.auspop.com.au/2015/02/damien-leith-new-album-tour/|title=DAMIEN LEITH : NEW ALBUM, TOUR|publisher=auspop.com.au|date=9 February 2015|access-date=10 February 2015|archive-date=10 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210015036/http://www.auspop.com.au/2015/02/damien-leith-new-album-tour/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2016, Leith will travel Australia with the "Winner’s Journey: 10th Anniversary Tour". Leith said; "It is hard to believe that it has been 10 years since I first stepped onto the 'Australian Idol stage'. One thing is for certain, I wouldn’t be doing what I am today without all the amazing support from fans over the years. From my albums, to my books and concerts, you've been there all the way and I can't thank you all enough."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.auspop.com.au/2016/05/damien-leith-10th-anniversary-tour/|title=DAMIEN LEITH 10TH ANNIVERSARY TOUR|publisher=auspop.com.au|date=2 May 2016|access-date=2 May 2016|archive-date=3 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160503090047/https://www.auspop.com.au/2016/05/damien-leith-10th-anniversary-tour/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In January 2017, Leith won his first [[Golden Guitar]] award at the [[Country Music Awards of Australia]] winning Song of the Year for "Call Me Cray" which he co-wrote with [[Travis Collins]]. In 2017, Leith toured the 'Roy – A Tribute to Roy Orbison' show across Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://music.theaureview.com/interviews/damien-leith-talks-music-legends-and-similarities-between-irish-country-music/|title=Damien Leith talks music legends and similarities between Irish & Country music|publisher=The AU Review|date=22 February 2017 |access-date=6 May 2018}}</ref>

===2018: ''Damien Leith Storytime'' and ''Gospel''===
In 2018 Leith commenced a new project called 'Damien Leith Storytime' and features bedtime stories for kids.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://damienleith.com.au/bio|title=Bio|publisher=Damien Leith|access-date=6 May 2018|archive-date=10 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180310120906/https://damienleith.com.au/bio|url-status=dead}}</ref> He released an EP in February. In August, Leith released his ninth studio album, ''Gospel''; an album inspired by [[Elvis Presley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jbhifi.com.au/music/browse/pop/gospel/313127/|title=Gospel|publisher=JBHiFi|access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref>

As of late August 2018, Leith joined [[Muswellbrook, New South Wales|Muswellbrook]]-based radio station [[98.1 Power FM]] as a breakfast announcer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.newmedia.com.au/index.html|title=Damien Leith Now on Radio|last=Newman|first=Greg|date=27 August 2018|website=Jock's Journal|access-date=11 September 2018|archive-date=10 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180910113205/http://www.newmedia.com.au/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2020, Leith performed "[[Uninvited (song)|Uninvited]]" with [[Greg Gould]] from Gould's album ''1998''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/au/album/1998/1497536509|title=1998 album|website=Apple Music|date=April 2020|access-date= May 12, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He was born in Ireland and raised near [[Milltown, County Kildare]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Irish singer is Australian Idol finalist |url=https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/2006/0919/407889-australianidol/ |date=19 September 2006 |publisher=[[RTÉ]] |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> His father travelled as part of his work as an engineer, and their family lived in various countries including [[Libya]] and [[Botswana]].<ref name="Biography">{{cite web|title=Damien Leith Biography |url=http://www.damienleith.com.au/biography/home.do |access-date=27 November 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061207031730/http://www.damienleith.com.au/biography/home.do |archive-date=7 December 2006 }}</ref>

Leith later on emigrated to Australia where he married Eileen Stapleton, an Australian. They have two sons and a daughter.<ref name="Oz Idol Damien Leith's baby joy">{{cite news|title=Oz Idol Damien Leith's baby joy|url=http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0,22049,20943375-5006009,00.html|access-date=18 December 2006|work=The Daily Telegraph|first=Kathy|last=McCabe|date=18 December 2006|archive-date=31 December 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121231053647/http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/news/sydney-news/oz-idol-damien-leiths-baby-joy/story-e6freuzi-1111112703403|url-status=dead}}</ref> Leith became an Australian citizen on 25 January 2007, taking the pledge from then Prime Minister of Australia, [[John Howard]], in a nationally televised broadcast on Network Ten.<ref>[http://www.thewest.com.au/aapstory.aspx?StoryName=336424 Irish Leith enjoying life as Aussie Idol (AAP 2006)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927192556/http://www.thewest.com.au/aapstory.aspx?StoryName=336424 |date=27 September 2007 }}. Retrieved 28 November 2006</ref> He currently lives in [[Wollongong, New South Wales]] and works as a radio announcer.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}
